page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with a 1.0 thread-per-core configuration. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and operates on a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance in the lower performance tiers. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is rated as weak, falling in the bottom 25%, while multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores register in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also place the instance in the bottom 10% tier. Cryptographic, compression, and database operations, such as Redis SET and PassMark database tests, consistently perform in the lower 10% range.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.large is its high memory allocation relative to its limited processing power and baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps. While the dedicated CPU allocation provides consistent execution, the overall low benchmark scores suggest it is not suited for compute-intensive tasks. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this profile is best utilized for lightweight, memory-dependent workloads that do not require high CPU throughput or local disk storage, such as small-scale caching, basic web serving, or low-traffic database operations.
